rv.q: At its best Richard Hawley and Chris Bush's musical love letter to Sheffield is a thing of elemental power.
Robert Hastie's superb production, on Ben Stones's soaring set, orchestrates all this beautifully, overlapping the stories to revealing or playful effect.
This stylish production set on the iconic Park Hill estate is a terrific blend of power and heart.
A deeply moving, monumental musical that really matters … deserves to be a huge hit.
It's jubilant and defiant, with the emotional force of a juggernaut.
This saga of three generations living in a brutalist Sheffield high-rise estate is something special.
Who'd have guessed a musical about Sheffield's brutalist Park Hill housing estate could be so uplifting?

Richard Hawley pulls on the heartstrings in his Sheffield opus … This new musical traces the intersecting lives of three families on the Park Hill estate in this spine-tingling and sentimental love song to the steel city … Directed by Robert Hastie, it looks at first like it is relishing a little too much in its theatricality as the three sets o...
It's a stirring tribute to the resili[ence]...

A love letter to community with backbone of steel … It’s an odd hybrid, part musical, part soap opera... a sincere if uneven love letter to the power of community. … In a way, the show is the blue-collar equivalent of Plaza Suite, the venerable Neil Simon comedy currently being revived at the Savoy.
Yet this often lovely piece of theatre also falls short of its own ambition.
A soaring achievement with new edges for the West End … The hit musical is as brilliant as ever as it moves to the Theatre.
This beautiful show breaks my heart and fills my soul … I've said it before, this is the greatest new British musical for years.

A joyful, gritty show with fire in its heart … A musical set on a Sheffield housing estate may not be the easiest pitch to Broadway producers - but they'd be missing out on the best British musical in decades. … Singer/songwriter Richard Hawley and playwright Chris Bush have fashioned a work that is both site-specific and universally epic.
